meeting_header:
Date: 2026-01-18
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood participants: Ava Chen, Liam Ortega, Sofia Patel
Greystone participants: Marcus Reed, Nina Harper, Ethan Soto
summary: Renewal check-in covering Greystone's upcoming renewal in Q1. Customer is leaning toward a 12-month renewal with a Dedicated pool in EU and a smaller Dedicated burst in US-West. Main concerns: EU latency, cost tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Hosted, KMS/encryption and audit logs. Action items: Redwood to send amended quote with Dedicated pricing and burst policy; Redwood SE to run latency benchmarks against Greystone prompt set in EU staging; customer to share prompt set and procurement timeline. Follow-up demo/benchmark readout scheduled next week.
topics: EU region onramp and latency expectations
questions: What will tail latency look like in the EU with our 4-token avg and 90th percentile targets?
Can you isolate EU data to our VPC and integrate with our KMS?
How does burst billing work when using Dedicated + Hosted fallback?
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Marcus (Greystone): Marcus here. Nina and Ethan on my side as well.
[00:11] Ava: Great, Ava here, Liam and Sofia from Redwood with me. We'll run through renewal, capacity, and the EU onramp.
[00:20] Nina: Quick note — we got the preliminary renewal doc, thanks. We're mainly worried about latency in EU, and cost.
[00:28] Liam (Redwood SE): Totally. We already flagged a couple of options — Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 with a small reserved commit, plus hosted fallback for burst. That gives predictable baseline throughput while letting you absorb spikes.
[00:39] Marcus: Right, budget's tight but we can't accept more than a 120ms tail, 95th p maybe?
[00:45] Liam: Ok, so couple of clarifiers: is that 95th over token generation or end-to-end request?
[00:50] Nina: End-to-end; user-facing. 4 tokens average per request in our chat flow but with occasional 200-token reports.
[00:58] Liam: Got it, those tail cases matter. For 200-token sequences in EU we'll likely see higher medians; we'll set up a bench to capture 50/95/99 pcts.
[01:08] Marcus: Can you give us an example SLA shift for Dedicated vs Hosted? Like, if we do Dedicated reserved 20k RUs per hour, what changes?
[01:17] Ava: With Dedicated you get capacity isolation and an SLA for throughput — latency targets are tighter because you have guaranteed GPU pool. Hosted fallback is cheaper for ephemeral spikes but you may see slightly higher tail latency under heavy global load.
[01:28] Ethan (Greystone Procurement): For procurement, we need to see the firm numbers — MRR impact and how burst is invoiced. Is burst metered? Is it a separate line item?
[01:36] Sofia (CSM): Burst is typically metered as overage on top of reserved commitment; we can show an example amortized monthly cost with a few scenarios in the quote.
[01:44] Marcus: Also, data residency — we need EU-only processing for certain customer classes. How does Redwood ensure requests originating from EU stay in EU?
[01:52] Liam: We provide region routing policies. If you pick EU region as primary and block failover outside EU for a route, requests route to eu nodes. For Dedicated we can pin instances to your EU pool. For Hosted fallback you'd need to allow global fallback or risk failing requests — though we can limit to compatible EU-hosted variants.
[02:06] Nina: KMS integration — we use a managed HSM. Can Redwood plug into our KMS for key wrapping?
[02:12] Liam: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated setups; for hosted we offer an envelope model but can also work with dedicated keys via our enterprise integration. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[02:25] Marcus: Ok, that helps. One more: audit logs. We need packet-level audit + token-level usage logs for compliance.
[02:31] Sofia: We can enable detailed audit logs and longer retention as an add-on. We'll include retention tiers in the quote.
[02:38] Marcus: Cool.
[02:41] [03:00] Liam: I want to propose a short benchmark: you send us a 10k sample prompt set and we run it in eu staging with Dedicated config (x nodes), capturing 50/95/99 latencies and cost per token. We'll also show a hosted fallback run to compare.
[03:15] Nina: We'll do that. We'll also send QPS curves, because our traffic bursts are spiky, 8k QPS for 90s then quiet.
[03:23] Liam: Good — that QPS shape helps us pick batching and pre-warm strategies.
[03:29] Ethan: Procurement question — term length? We're thinking 12 months but want flexibility to add capacity mid-term. Is there an amendment process?
[03:36] Ava: Yes, 12-month term is standard. You can add capacity mid-term via commitment amendments. We can include a tiered discount schedule for commit bands to show cost benefits.
[03:46] Marcus: What's the earliest we can activate EU Dedicated nodes if we sign?
[03:49] Sofia: Typical lead time for EU Dedicated is 2-3 weeks from PO and onboarding paperwork; for on-prem or Private it's longer.
[03:56] Marcus: 2-3 weeks is acceptable.
[04:00] [05:00] Ava: On pricing specifics, I'll propose two options in the amendment: (A) 12-month reserved commit with Dedicated EU pool and hosted fallback for bursts, (B) a hybrid with smaller reserved commit plus larger hosted fallback to reduce MRR. We'll include example monthly costs and projected overage under your traffic profile.
[05:18] Marcus: Option B might be attractive given budget constraints, but we need to see tail-latency tradeoffs.
[05:24] Liam: We'll quantify that in the benchmark. Note that batching parameters can reduce per-token cost but add latency for single-shot calls; we'll show different batching configs.
[05:34] Nina: Are there any model quantization recommendations that affect quality for our summarization workloads? We care about accuracy.
[05:40] Liam: For summarization we recommend fp16 or 4-bit with per-channel quantization on the dedicated nodes; Redwood Optimize will suggest quant profiles against a holdout prompt set. We'll avoid aggressive quant for critical flows.
[05:52] [06:00] Marcus: Great. Security: we need SSO/SAML into Console and granular RBAC for routes and keys.
[06:06] Sofia: We support SSO/SAML and RBAC. We'll share a sample role matrix and the onboarding checklist.
[06:12] Ethan: For procurement, what's the billing cadence — monthly or annual? We prefer monthly but can commit annual if we get better rates.
[06:19] Ava: Both options are available. Annual commitment triggers a larger discount; monthly gives you more flexibility. We'll show both in the amendment.
[06:26] [07:00] Matthew (mislabelled Speaker 2): I think you also asked about egress charges?
[07:04] Marcus: Yes, if we keep data in EU and export embeddings for downstream analytics, are there egress fees?
[07:10] Liam: Egress is charged per region egress policy; if you process and store embeddings in EU and export them out, there's a standard egress line; we'll call that out explicitly.
[07:18] Nina: Could we do a data transfer pipeline to S3 in EU to avoid cross-region egress?
[07:23] Liam: Yes, we can stage outputs into your EU bucket; we'll include recommended patterns.
[07:27] [08:00] Marcus: Ok back to timeline: Nina will send prompt set by Tuesday?
[08:04] Nina: Yes, I'll send it by 2026-01-19 EOD.
[08:08] Liam: Great, I'll queue up the EU staging run and aim to share raw numbers and a short write-up by 2026-01-26.
[08:15] Ava: I'll prepare the renewal amendment and pricing scenarios and target sending by 2026-01-22.
[08:21] Ethan: Procurement will aim to have PO approvals by 2026-01-29 if numbers align.
[08:27] [09:00] Marcus: On SLA — do you have credits or remedies for missed latency SLOs?
[09:05] Sofia: We can include latency and availability SLAs with service credits; our standard enterprise contracts include credit formulas. We'll propose language in the amendment.
[09:14] Marcus: Ok. Also curious about canarying new model versions — we run A/B for quality checks.
[09:20] Liam: Canary and rollout policies are supported. You can pin particular model versions to routes, do a % rollout and automatic fallback to previous model on regressions. We'll show the Console flow.
[09:31] Nina: For Private deployment (VPC/on-prem), what's the rough timeline if we needed it?
[09:36] Ava: Private on-prem is a longer process — typically 8-12 weeks including packaging, networking, and compliance review. But Dedicated in EU is much faster and covers most needs.
[09:46] [10:00] Marcus: If we sign for Dedicated, do we get dedicated TLS certs and KV cache isolation?
[10:02] Liam: Yes, TLS certs and KV cache is isolated to your pool. There are some nuances with multi-tenant hashed caches but with Dedicated everything stays within your instance.
[10:12] Marcus: Any gotchas around prefix caching or session warmers? We have a lot of short-lived sessions.
[10:18] Liam: Prefix/KV caching works well for repeated contexts; for short-lived sessions, pre-warm and continuous batching techniques help. We'll recommend a pre-warm schedule in the bench write-up.
[10:27] [12:00] Ava: Ok let's do a quick recap and confirm owners. Ava to send amendment (due 1/22), Liam to run bench (due 1/26), Nina to send prompt set (due 1/19), Ethan to confirm procurement timeline (due 1/21). Any other items?
[12:45] Marcus: Might be good to do a short follow-up readout after the benchmark. Can we schedule 30 minutes?
[12:50] Ava: Yes — tentative slot Wednesday 2026-01-28 15:00 UTC. We'll send calendar invite after we post results.
[12:58] Nina: Also please include a sample incident playbook for failover from Dedicated to Hosted fallback.
[13:05] Sofia: We'll include the failover playbook and runbook excerpt.
[13:10] [14:00] Ethan: Procurement will likely ask for our standard MSA redlines; what is the typical turn-around?
[14:08] Ava: We can do a legal turnaround in 7-10 business days once we have a signed LOI/PO. We'll include standard MSA and SOW templates with the amendment.
[14:18] Marcus: Great. One quick technical — are you able to enforce region affinity at the route level for specific customer segments?
[14:24] Liam: Yes, routing policies can be configured per-route with priority rules and fallbacks. We'll show a config snippet in the write-up.
[14:30] [16:00] Nina: Also, curious about observability — per-token cost breakdowns and tracing into our app?
[16:06] Sofia: We provide token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns, and tracing hooks that integrate with OpenTelemetry to correlate requests in your stack.
[16:14] Marcus: Perfect.
[16:17] [20:00] Ava: Anything else before we close?
[20:03] Marcus: That's about it. Thanks, everyone.
[20:07] Ava: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs and quote. Talk soon.
[20:12] [47:30] Meeting ends.
